title: CI-tested zero-install browser fallback (Binder/repo2docker + Colab/Posit Cloud/Codespaces)
context: PLAN.md v0.2 promotes a zero-install browser fallback from an afterthought to a first-class, M0-exit deliverable. A learner on a low-spec or Windows machine must never need to debug a local install. The plan mandates: Binder/repo2docker as primary path; Colab / Posit Cloud / Codespaces as named fallbacks; webR / JupyterLite evaluated for install-free R/Python; and all paths CI-tested against explicit MB/RAM/cold-load-time budgets. No single hosted service may be a hard dependency. This task is an M0 exit criterion per PLAN.md v0.2.
objective: Deliver a CI-tested zero-install browser fallback: a repo2docker configuration (apt.txt, runtime.txt or environment.yml binder/) that launches a working Quarto/R/Python environment on mybinder.org, documented fallback instructions for Colab / Posit Cloud / Codespaces, an evaluation note on webR/JupyterLite viability, and a CI step that builds the Binder image (or image manifest) and asserts declared MB/RAM/cold-load budgets are met.
acceptanceCriteria: A repo2docker / Binder configuration (binder/ directory) is committed and launches a working dual-track (R + Python) environment on mybinder.org without manual setup.
Documented fallback paths (Colab, Posit Cloud, Codespaces) with launch links or one-click badges, so no single hosted service is a hard dependency.
A written evaluation note (inline or in docs/) covers webR and JupyterLite viability for install-free R/Python and why each is or is not adopted.
Declared MB/RAM/cold-load-time budgets are committed as constants (e.g., in a binder/budgets.yml or CI env vars) and a CI step asserts the Binder image build stays within them.
CI step fails the build if the Binder image exceeds declared MB/RAM budgets or cold-load-time target.
